scope: Engineering and control research lead: first-wave attacks plus Cycle 2 directed finite-volume switching certificate and costed guarded birth/death relay. Model-level proofs, source-reported results, exact finite computations, novelty, and physical validation remain separate statuses.

assumptions: The phase universe includes M distinct competing structures at the candidate composition.
A hidden phase may have energy -(tau+eta), with tau>=0 and eta>0.
The oracle reveals only the queried phase's exact energy.
No sound energy lower bounds, complete phase hull, or structure-search certificate are supplied.
UNKNOWN/abstention counts as failure to decide.
claims.novelty_boundary: A finite-oracle indistinguishability argument specialized to competing polymorphs and energy-above-hull feasibility. No priority claim; the result does not apply when a complete hull or certified lower bounds are supplied.
claims.costs: At least M competitor energy queries worst-case for deterministic zero-error decisions, or expected c_E M(1-2 delta) under the stated randomized guarantee and equal query cost. Structure generation, DFT relaxation cost, target-property evaluation, hull LP cost, training, and experiments are additional.
claims.falsifier: Under the exact stated oracle contract, return a correct hard feasibility decision on every constructed world without querying all competitors or acquiring a sound lower-bound service.
claims.next_gate: Instrument a phase family with multiple polymorphs and verify that all feasibility labels consume either competitor energies or a documented sound lower-bound/full-hull service.
claims.exact_statement: For a candidate x at composition c0 with E_x=0 and known zero-energy binary endpoints, if there are M unqueried possible competing polymorphs at c0, exact point-energy queries are the only information source, no lower bounds are supplied, and the algorithm must decide FEASIBLE versus INFEASIBLE, then every zero-error deterministic algorithm needs M competitor queries in the worst case. Any randomized algorithm with error at most delta on the all-zero world and each single-hidden-low-polymorph world requires expected at least M(1-2 delta) competitor queries on the all-zero world for delta<1/2. For equal per-query cost c_E, expected energy-evaluation cost is at least c_E M(1-2 delta).

assumptions: The composition-feasible convex-mixture set is fixed under the perturbation.
The energy error bound is simultaneous and uniform over candidate and all competing phases.
The same reference-energy convention and normalization are used for all phase energies.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard convex-mixture stability argument applied to hull-gap classification; no claim of a new general convex-analysis theorem.
claims.costs: Computing hull bounds requires an LP/convex-hull operation over acquired phases. Obtaining uniform simultaneous energy intervals is an upstream data/model-acquisition cost and is not supplied by an average test MAE.
claims.falsifier: A fixed phase universe and uniform sup-norm perturbation with a hull value changing by more than epsilon, or a gap changing by more than 2 epsilon.
claims.next_gate: Measure family-held-out, simultaneous energy bounds and test whether they support the declared hull threshold margins.
claims.exact_statement: For a fixed finite phase/composition universe, if every relevant per-atom phase energy changes by at most epsilon in sup norm, then the convex-hull energy at every composition changes by at most epsilon and any candidate-minus-competing-hull gap changes by at most 2 epsilon. A threshold label is invariant when the gap margin exceeds 2 epsilon.

assumptions: The finite phase universe is explicitly declared and contains all admissible competitors for the stated scope.
All intervals have simultaneous coverage; marginal coverage alone is insufficient without correction.
Composition vectors and energy normalization are consistent.
claims.novelty_boundary: Robust LP enclosure is a proposed interface and acquisition component; no convergence, efficiency, or novelty claim.
claims.costs: Per candidate: two LPs over the current phase pool, plus interval-model fitting and phase energy acquisition. A phase query may update hull bounds for many target compositions and must be costed once, with shared value credited.
claims.falsifier: For any energy realization within all supplied intervals, the computed FEASIBLE/INFEASIBLE classification violates the stated threshold condition.
claims.next_gate: Implement exact small-pool LPs, then compare the query schedule against an equally informed cost-aware point-label BO baseline on held-out phase families.
claims.exact_statement: Given simultaneous valid intervals L_y<=E_y<=U_y for every phase in a declared finite phase universe, LPs minimizing mixture energy using L and U bound the true competing-phase hull. U_x-H^-_x<=tau is a sufficient robust feasibility condition; L_x-H^+_x>tau is a sufficient robust infeasibility condition; otherwise return UNKNOWN.

assumptions: Source description is accurately transcribed from the local arXiv v2 PDF.
A random-record MAE is not promoted to a uniform or simultaneous bound.
claims.status: source-reported; locally read; not independently replayed; transfer to hard feasibility unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: The paper's empirical low-facet findings and transfer claims are author-reported. This work makes no priority claim and does not dispute the empirical dataset metrics.
claims.costs: Reported model fitting: Adam, batch 512, 1,600 epochs. Source does not report comparable end-to-end model runtime or charge acquisition of the seed Materials Project data. Full DFT and held-out family-validation costs remain unknown.
claims.falsifier: A source-provided, independently replayed simultaneous uniform error guarantee over the candidate and all relevant phase competitors, strong enough to decide the stated cutoff.
claims.next_gate: Acquire family-held-out error intervals and verify error on candidate-minus-hull gaps, including omitted polymorphs and finite-temperature/kinetic exclusions.
claims.exact_statement: The read arXiv v2 manuscript reports a seven-facet max-affine fit in 92 composition coordinates with 0.076 eV/atom random 20% holdout MAE on 51,068 near-hull Materials Project compounds; this result supplies neither a uniform energy-error bound nor a candidate-wise hull-gap guarantee at a 0.05 eV/atom cutoff.

For xdot=A x+B u with known A,B,x(0), no process disturbance, passive state sensor y=Cx, and an actuator independent of sensor enable z, every causal finite-cost sensor/controller policy can be replayed with z=0 and identical state and actuator paths. If cost is integral(x'Qx+u'Ru+s z)dt with s>0, replay saves exactly s integral z dt. Hence no positive-duration sensing policy is optimal in this interface.
assumptions: A, B, and x(0) known to controller
deterministic plant with unique trajectories
no process noise, unknown disturbance, parameter drift, or unknown initial state
sensor output is passive and does not affect plant
actuator remains independently commandable when sensor is off
internal prediction and simulation carry no cost
claims.status: internally reconstructed theorem; not externally reviewed
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a model degeneracy / counterexample for pure sensing costs in deterministic known-state plants, not a new scheduler and not a result about stochastic event-triggered LQG. A hard z=0=>u=0 interlock changes the interface to coupled sensor/actuator co-scheduling.

costs.sensing: s joules per second if z is physically on-time and units are calibrated; total s integral z dt
costs.actuation: integral u'Ru dt, retained exactly by replay
costs.state: integral x'Qx dt, retained exactly by replay
costs.computation: assumed free; model-prediction cost is not included

claims.falsifier: With a calibrated known plant and initial state, measure sensor-off predictor residual x_meas-x_hat while replaying actions. A reproducible residual beyond numerical and measurement tolerance, or a sensor/actuator interlock, violates an assumption and invalidates the dominance conclusion for that plant/interface.
claims.next_gate: Add process noise or bounded model uncertainty and separate sensor and actuator controls; compare to event-triggered LQG under the same observation charge, actuator cost, noise law, and information pattern.

claims.exact_statement: In Tran-Ngo-Das 2026's fixed-gain scalar switching model, a=-1,b=1,k=1/2,q1=1,r=1,q2=r k^2=1/4,s=1/10,x0=1 satisfies Proposition 2 and gives t_sw=ln(0.4)/(-3)=0.30543024 and restricted objective J=0.48054302. Independent-actuator full-information LQR for xdot=-x+u with q=r=1 has J*=sqrt(2)-1=0.41421356 and zero sensing cost.
assumptions: Tran-Ngo-Das deterministic scalar known-state model and Proposition 2 hypotheses
fixed-gain source policy has z=1 then z=0 with u=0 when z=0
comparator allows independent actuator control and exact internal state propagation
claims.status: exact calculation from source model; conditional interface comparison
claims.novelty_boundary: The numeric comparison does not refute Proposition 2 within its fixed-gain, sensor-gates-actuator class. It shows that this class is strictly weaker than an independently actuated controller with the same deterministic model information.
claims.falsifier: Enforce and verify a physical interlock z=0=>u=0; then the no-sensor LQR comparator is not feasible and this conditional gap no longer applies.
claims.next_gate: Determine whether a target engineering system has independent sensor and actuator enables; if yes, use model-based replay as the baseline, otherwise model the joint enable cost explicitly.

claims.exact_statement: For the finite-volume birth-death relay V=100 with H rates lambda_plus=2(100-n), lambda_minus=n and L rates lambda_plus=100-n, lambda_minus=2n, initialize H at n=45; switch H-to-L only at n=55 and L-to-H only at n=45; fault-stop at n=10 or 90 or after a one-second per-leg deadline. The exact per-leg deadline success probability is p(t)=e_45^T integral_0^t exp(Q_H s)q_55 ds, identical in the reflected L leg, and M legs all succeed with probability p(t)^M by strong Markov regeneration. With no deadline but safety boundaries, p_infinity=P_45(tau_55<tau_10)=31093519817410066218136533805526688768/31093519817410066218136534504523754857<1; thus infinite safe recurrence has probability zero. For every fixed t>0, probability of no reaction during an H leg's first t seconds is exp(-155t)>0, so probability-one fixed-period guard attainment is impossible. The exact rational resolvent from n=45 until hitting 10 or 55 gives mean duration 0.18942271777417605 s, expected H births 19.29484785161174 and deaths 9.294847851611737. The one-second value p(1)=0.9999720896127573 and its 20-leg product are floating-point uniformization outputs with Poisson truncation error <=5.4805307045e-51, not roundoff-certified.
assumptions: Exact CTMC model with integer copy number n and calibrated, time-homogeneous mass-action rates as stated.
Every molecule transition is observed without delay or missed events; control switches instantaneously at the stated singleton guard.
Strong Markov property and independent future reaction noise conditional on the current copy number and mode.
The safe band is 10<=n<=90; target hit and unsafe hit are absorbing for one-leg analysis.
For deadline calculation, fault-stop at the earlier of safe target hit, unsafe-boundary hit, and one-second timeout.

Illustrative costs only: P_s=20mW, P_c=5mW, P_m=100mW continuously while a leg is active; E_obs=1mJ and E_cpu=0.2mJ per observed transition; E_birth=0.5mJ and E_death=0.2mJ per corresponding molecular event; E_sw=50mJ per successful switch. No fault-shutdown charge is included unless separately measured and added as E_f*(1-p_hit).
claims.status: conditional finite-state construction and exact rational resolvent; one-second probability is internally computed floating-point uniformization, not interval-certified; no external review
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a narrow finite-state CTMC construction, concentration/reachability computation, and cost accounting example. It is not a new concentration inequality, a probability-one periodic-control theorem, or a novelty/priority claim. The 2021 Anand-Jagtap-Zamani source explicitly models bounded Lipschitz state-dependent CTMC mode-switching intensities for a diffusion; it does not analyze this chemical-jump relay. The 2026 publisher abstract describes instantaneous jumps with constrained inter-jump times, but the available abstract does not establish state-dependent CTMC mode intensities.

costs.continuous_holding: (P_s+P_c+P_m)*sum_n o_n(t), where o_n is expected transient occupation up to target, unsafe boundary, or deadline; this charges holding power through the full one-leg duration.
costs.event_sensing_and_processing: sum_n o_n(t)*(E_obs+E_cpu)*(lambda_plus(n)+lambda_minus(n)); counts transitions including jumps into absorbing target/unsafe states.
costs.chemical_event_energy: sum_n o_n(t)*(E_birth*lambda_plus(n)+E_death*lambda_minus(n)); reflection swaps birth/death counts, so H and L expected costs can differ when E_birth != E_death.
costs.successful_mode_switch: E_sw*p_hit(t), not E_sw unconditionally; add E_fault*(1-p_hit(t)) only if failure shutdown consumes that measured energy.
costs.multi_leg_expected_cost: C_1+p_1*C_2+p_1*p_2*C_3+... with each C_j the full attempted-leg expected cost and each p_j the target-safe hit probability; use alternating H/L costs when per-event prices are asymmetric.

claims.falsifier: A probability-one fixed-deadline guard claim is falsified by the no-reaction path, which the stated model assigns probability exp(-155t). The finite-time subgenerator claim is falsified if preregistered calibrated trials produce hit-before-unsafe frequency below its predicted value outside the stated confidence interval. The energy claim is falsified if measured holding power, event counts/work, successful switches, and any fault shutdown charge exceed the occupancy-weighted cost expression after measurement uncertainty is included.
claims.next_gate: Acquire a calibrated V=100 reaction system with transition-resolved sensing; if optional switching, rate modulation, or alternate modes are permitted, specify that action set and compare with a matching timed CTMDP or Markov-renewal controller.

claims.exact_statement: Under the exact Cycle-2 relay interface—fixed H/L propensities, full observation, H held until its first hit of n=55, L held until its first hit of n=45, immediate mode switch at each target, and fault-stop at the stated unsafe boundary or one-second deadline—the admissible feedback-policy set is a singleton. Therefore every finite-state CTMDP comparator restricted to the same actions has the same timed reach probability and expected cost as the fixed-policy CTMC. This is interface-relative evaluation, not optimality among controllers with rate modulation, optional/delayed guard switches, or alternate actions. A resettable per-leg deadline is a continuous timer; the exact finite-leg computation uses one-leg semigroup/occupancy kernels and strong-Markov recursion rather than asserting a homogeneous finite-state CTMDP representation.
assumptions: The controller must hold the specified mode until the first target-guard hit; switching at that hit is mandatory and instantaneous.
No mode/rate choice, waiting decision within the guard, control-induced state reset, or alternate failure response is allowed.
The current molecule count, mode, and transition times are observed exactly; observations do not add control options.
Each one-second deadline resets only after a successful target-guard switch; failure stops the experiment.
claims.status: internally proved from the declared action interface; no claim about an expanded controller class
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a policy-class degeneracy statement. Uniform CTMDP optimization has no effect when every admissible action set is a singleton; it does not prove the guard relay is optimal once optional switching, mode selection, or rate control is permitted.

costs.holding: Sensor, clock/controller, and mode-hold power are integrated over transient occupancy until hit, unsafe exit, or deadline.
costs.events: Sensing/processing and birth/death event charges are rate-weighted by the same transient occupancy, including absorbing jumps.
costs.switch: Charge E_sw*p_hit for successful target arrival only; add measured fault energy E_f*(1-p_hit) if applicable.
costs.multi_leg: C_1+p_1*C_2+...+product_{i<M}p_i*C_M with distinct alternating H/L costs if birth/death prices differ.

claims.falsifier: The singleton conclusion fails if the physical or specified controller can choose at least two distinct actions in any reachable state/history while meeting the same guard/deadline rules (for example, rate modulation, optional/delayed switching inside a guard, or a mode choice). The numerical CTMC evaluation is separately falsified by calibrated transition-resolved statistics or measured energy outside preregistered tolerances.
claims.next_gate: If a nontrivial action set is intended, enumerate it exactly—including when actions can be selected, deadline behavior, and costs—then solve the corresponding timed CTMDP or Markov-renewal control problem; do not compare against unconstrained uniformized schedulers.

claims.exact_statement: For xdot=u, y=x^2+v on [0,T], with x0 in [-R,R], precommitted open-loop measurable u, exact known input/model, deterministic ||v||_infinity<=delta, and integral_0^T u^2 dt<=E, if R>=sqrt(E*T)/2+delta/sqrt(E*T), every finite-sample or full-trace estimator has worst-case absolute error at least delta/sqrt(E*T). The constant input u=sqrt(E/T) and endpoint estimator (y(T)-y(0)-E*T)/(2*sqrt(E*T)) attain the bound. The exact claim excludes process and model error and does not cover adaptive sensing policies.
assumptions: scalar integrator and quadratic sensor are supplied exactly
the probe is selected before observations
the input trace and displacement are known exactly
sensor noise is adversarial but bounded by delta in absolute value
initial interval contains the two indistinguishable states as ensured by the stated R condition
claims.novelty_boundary: A sharp scalar specialization of finite-horizon set-valued observability and active trajectory design. No evidence establishes novelty or priority beyond current robust MHE and output-feedback control baselines.

costs.measurements: 2 endpoint readings at effective absolute precision delta for the attaining algorithm; lower bound grants the full output trace
costs.excitation: probe energy E_p=D^2/T and displacement D=sqrt(E_p*T); safety and actuator limits separately require D<=S-R and D<=Umax*T
costs.runtime: constant-size scalar arithmetic and one division; total control horizon T+Tc
costs.supplied_inputs: plant law, sensor origin/law, calibration, and exact control logging

claims.falsifier: Under certified exact integrator dynamics, known displacement D, and endpoint errors each <=delta, a measured estimator error greater than delta/D falsifies the exact formula; otherwise unmodeled displacement/noise must fit the explicit enlarged bound in the proof.
claims.next_gate: Determine whether the exact minimax law is already an immediate consequence of Deole-Mesbahi set-valued observability or standard minimax set-membership control; only then attempt a sharp vector/state-dependent-noise extension.

claims.exact_statement: For u=0 and y=x^2, the initial states +a and -a are indistinguishable for every time and any noise-free estimator, so worst-case state error over an interval containing both is at least a.
assumptions: state is constant under zero input
sensor law is y=x^2
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary symmetry obstruction; it instantiates the distinction between local/controlled observability and an unexcited output trajectory.

costs.data: arbitrarily many exact output readings do not break the symmetry
costs.runtime: not relevant; the observation maps coincide

claims.falsifier: An exact output trace under zero input that differs for +a and -a would contradict the stated sensor/dynamics model.
claims.next_gate: Use as a falsifier for any observer guarantee that omits an excitation or distinguishability assumption.

claims.exact_statement: For q_t + c q_x = 0 on [0,L], with q(0,t)=u(t), nonnegative q0 bounded by Q, an unknown time-constant c in a certified interval [c_-,c_+], and nonnegative zero-order-hold controls of period h bounded by U_max, if the controller knows initial cell integrals, uses the upper envelope for all within-cell profiles consistent with those integrals and Q, and at each sample chooses a command satisfying A_k^+(c,s)+B(c,s)a <= M_max for every admitted c and every elapsed s in [0,h], then total inventory M_c(t)=integral_0^L q(x,t) dx remains at most M_max for all t. The continuous supremum gives the largest command robust over the acquired profile class; the stated speed-time grid with its Lipschitz margin gives a conservative certified implementation.
assumptions: Scalar linear transport with constant-in-time positive speed; c is uncertain only within a fixed certified compact interval.
No diffusion, reaction, recirculation, time-varying coefficient, or unmodeled source.
Initial state is nonnegative and bounded by known Q; cell integrals are acquired with known measurement-error intervals.
Boundary input is nonnegative, bounded, and held constant on each interval of length h.
Initial inventory is certified below M_max; finite-precision evaluations round mass upper bounds upward and commands downward.
claims.novelty_boundary: Prior art includes delay-state control barrier functionals, continuum CBF/backstepping safety filters for Stefan PDEs, learned PDE boundary-output barriers, continuous-time safe output regulation for coupled hyperbolic PDE-ODE cascades, spatial CBFs for linearized LWR density, and adaptive output positivity for hyperbolic/parabolic PDE-ODE cascades. The candidate interface is plug-flow total inventory with uncertain fixed speed, acquired initial cell masses, held actuation, and a certified speed-time grid. No priority or novelty claim is established.

costs.acquisition: N initial cell-integral measurements, density bound Q, and certified speed interval. Optional ideal speed calibration uses at most ceil(tau_max/delta)+1 outlet readings and step effort A^2(tau_max+delta), multiplied by measured actuator coefficient kappa for energy.
costs.discretization: Within-cell partial-inventory ambiguity is at most Qd/2 per cut cell and is bounded sharply using cell mass and density cap. Speed-time gridding adds mass margin 0.5(K_c d_c + K_s d_s), plus measurement and arithmetic allowances.
costs.runtime: With n_c by n_s speed-time grid, N initial cells, and H=ceil(tau_max/h)+1 stored commands: O(n_c n_s log(N+H)) arithmetic and O(N+H) memory per sample using prefix arrays.
costs.effort: Normalized input effort is sum_k h a_k^2. Physical energy requires a measured power law P=kappa u^2; no physical energy is claimed absent kappa.

claims.falsifier: A characteristic-simulator trace using an admitted speed, an admissible initial profile matching all measured cell integrals and Q, and a command accepted by the certified filter, yet with inventory exceeding M_max between samples.
claims.next_gate: Implement the interval-grid filter and adversarial partial-cell profiles; compare against no-grid exact filtering, sample-only inventory checks, and a delay-CBF baseline with matched speed bounds and sensing.

claims.exact_statement: For a cell of width d with 0 <= q0 <= Q and acquired cell mass m, the possible mass in a prefix of length r is exactly [max(0,m-Q(d-r)), min(m,Qr)]. The uncertainty width is at most Q min(r,d-r), and therefore at most Qd/2; the half-cell upper bound is attained for compatible cell mass and profile.
assumptions: The cell mass m is exact; with measurement error, use the certified interval upper endpoint.
The pointwise density cap 0 <= q0 <= Q is valid throughout the cell.
claims.novelty_boundary: Elementary extremal allocation of bounded density inside one cell; no novelty or priority claim.

costs.acquisition: One integral measurement per spatial cell, plus a valid Q bound.
costs.discretization: At most Qd/2 uncertainty for one partial-cell prefix; the full filter uses the exact mass-dependent upper endpoint.

claims.falsifier: A bounded density profile violating the stated interval while having the same cell integral, or a profile construction showing an endpoint unattainable under the assumptions.
claims.next_gate: Adversarially construct prefix-first and suffix-first profiles in the exact-characteristic simulator.

claims.exact_statement: After the initial wave clears, pure transport maps inlet signal to outlet as y(t)=u(t-tau). Without an input regularity bound, a pulse of height Y+epsilon and width below sample spacing delta can violate y<=Y between output samples while all sampled values are safe. If |u_dot|<=R and sample error is at most e_y, y(t_j)<=Y-R delta/2-e_y at every sample implies y(t)<=Y for all time; the R delta/2 margin is sharp under only the stated Lipschitz information.
assumptions: Pure constant-speed transport after initial profile has exited.
Output sample spacing is at most delta.
For the sufficient margin, inlet slew satisfies |u_dot| <= R and output measurement error is bounded by e_y.
claims.novelty_boundary: Standard Lipschitz sampling argument stated for a pure-delay transport output. It diagnoses the gap between sampled feasibility data and continuous-time safety; it does not refute a continuous-time barrier theorem whose hypotheses hold for every t.

costs.acquisition: Output sensor sampling every delta and a certified actuator slew bound R.
costs.runtime: One scalar margin check per sample.

claims.falsifier: A pulse counterexample meeting all regularity assumptions, or an intersample output above Y despite the stated sample margin.

claims.exact_statement: For N iid Bernoulli failure observations with unknown policy failure probability p, every uniformly valid one-sided (1-alpha) upper confidence bound U must satisfy U(0,...,0) >= epsilon whenever (1-epsilon)^N > alpha. Therefore certifying p <= epsilon after zero observed failures requires N >= ceil(log(alpha)/log(1-epsilon)).
assumptions: one fixed feedback policy is evaluated across independent reset runs
the model class contains the Bernoulli rare-shock family with observationally identical no-failure paths
no parametric transition model, valid likelihood ratio, or safety certificate is supplied
the confidence statement is uniform over p in [0,1]
claims.status: proved_here; standard exact-binomial content; no novelty claim
claims.novelty_boundary: This is a direct coverage argument and exact zero-count binomial limit, not a new confidence interval. The workstream contribution is its explicit application to frozen feedback-policy certification and matched cost accounting against supplied-certificate operation-time guarantees.

costs.transition_evaluations: H times the episode count for horizon H
costs.physical_testing: exposure failures consume a separate operational risk budget
costs.importance_sampling: requires a support-complete change of measure and computable likelihood ratios; otherwise not identified
costs.controller_compute: policy search, data reuse, trajectory generation, and any sequential correction must be charged separately

claims.falsifier: On the all-zero trajectory path, any purported uniformly valid bound below epsilon with (1-epsilon)^N > alpha has noncoverage greater than alpha under p=epsilon.
claims.next_gate: Add structure (known jump rates, a support-complete IS model, or a verifiable barrier) and compare the resulting policy against exact finite-horizon reachability under matched acquisition and compute budgets.

claims.exact_statement: For the supplied N35 closed two-species chain with fixed positive rates, the transient states A=1,...,V-1 form a finite irreducible class, so the chain visits A=1 almost surely; for even V>=6, this eventually exits Q=[V/4,3V/4]. Thus its certified exponentially long finite horizon does not imply all-time containment or stochastic permanence.
assumptions: the source N35 reaction example and its count-chain birth/death rates
fixed positive admissible reaction rates
closed class of total population V and V>=6
claims.status: reconstructed consequence of supplied source example; not new; external source theorem not validated
claims.novelty_boundary: The source proof already states the eventual-exit consequence. We independently checked the finite irreducible birth-death class argument to preserve the horizon scope.

costs.model: integer reaction complexes, exact count lattice, bounded reaction rates
costs.certificate: positive compact inward polytope and supplied initial buffer
costs.compute: equation (7) can certify long horizons while thinning work remains order V*T

claims.falsifier: For a fixed positive-rate example, failure of connected positive birth/death transitions on states 1,...,V-1 would invalidate the recurrence argument.
claims.next_gate: Treat finite horizon explicitly in any controller or risk-budget comparison; do not infer permanence from the exponential horizon.

claims.exact_statement: The N35 finite-volume exit bound is conditional on a supplied acquired strict inward-facet certificate, bounded predictable rate controls, and lattice-compatible buffered initial data; it is not a model-free rare-event estimator or a policy-synthesis algorithm.
assumptions: integer molecular reaction network and supplied stoichiometric lattice
compact positive polytope Q with supplied inward collar widths and margins for all admitted modes
bounded predictable rates and initial facet gaps bounded away from zero
explicit finite volume and horizon
claims.status: source-derived candidate, reconstructed from supplied full proof; external correctness and novelty unresolved
claims.novelty_boundary: Astra explicitly identifies this as an exponential-martingale application, not a new large-deviation principle; comparison to Agazzi-Dembo-Eckmann is retained. The source's internal diagnostics were not replayed.

costs.certificate_acquisition: finding and proving Q, collar widths, and margins may require costly nonlinear or quantifier-elimination work
costs.operation: rate/time, molecule volume/count storage, controller service and reaction turnover
costs.simulation: expected rate-V*Lambda thinning candidate count up to T is V*Lambda*T
costs.precision: rational constants, lattice compatibility, and propensity corrections are explicit

claims.falsifier: An admitted mode with nonpositive deterministic inward margin, an uncharged propensity correction, or an incompatible initial count invalidates direct application of the bound.
claims.next_gate: Develop and cost a certificate-acquisition/controller-synthesis service; compare its safety horizon and intervention cost to exact finite-state reachability and robust dynamic programming.

claims.exact_statement: For the scalar-integrator, fixed connected undirected graph, global shared-medium DoS, and self-triggered protocol specified by Senejohnny–Tesi–De Persis (2015), their stated condition 1/tau_d + Delta_*/tau_f < 1, with Delta_*=epsilon/(4 d_min), is sufficient for finite-time convergence to the practical-consensus set |ave_i|<epsilon for every node.
assumptions: All nodes and states are fault-free.
DoS disables all communication across one shared medium at once.
Fixed connected undirected graph; exact real-valued relative-state polling at local events.
DoS start-frequency and total-duration envelopes hold for every time interval.
claims.status: source-reported; interface and proof steps internally reconstructed
claims.novelty_boundary: Established source result as reported by the primary paper; not externally revalidated here. It does not cover independent per-link DoS or Byzantine nodes.
claims.costs: Per sample each node polls all d_i neighbors and computes ave_i; transmission, receive, sensor, trigger-computation, and actuation joules are not priced in the theorem.
claims.falsifier: A counterexample satisfying the paper's global shared-medium model and its stated frequency/duration bounds but not reaching the practical-consensus set would falsify this source claim.
claims.next_gate: Reconstruct full journal proof and distinguish its global channel model from any edge-wise extension.

claims.exact_statement: In a directed K4 with common retry interval delta=Delta_*=epsilon/12, if every receiver loses one incoming edge at each event and the missing edge rotates through its three in-neighbors, with each edge outage of duration rho=delta/10 recurring every 3 delta, then every edge satisfies the scalar PoC expression phi_e=11/30<1 while a fail-closed complete-neighborhood controller receives no complete neighbor vector at any event and remains at any post-transient state whose diameter exceeds epsilon.
assumptions: Four scalar agents, complete directed graph without self-links, synchronous event times.
At each event one incoming edge per receiver is unavailable; edge identities rotate with period three events.
Outage windows cover the event instant and last rho=delta/10.
The specified full-vector controller sets control to zero and retries after delta whenever any input is missing.
The state after the first failed event has diameter greater than epsilon.
claims.status: internally reconstructed counterexample; edge schedules and inequalities exact
